story.iWant: a pipeline that converts uploads (Markdown, PDF, HTML) into normalized Markdown chunks and embeddings
story.soThat: the memory store is consistent and ready for semantic search
story.tasks: - Task 1: Add CLI entrypoint for ingestion (AC: #1, #4) * Implement jarvis memory add <path> command with input validation and format detection * Integrate pandoc conversion for PDF/HTML to Markdown; no-op for Markdown inputs * Ensure metadata (source path, section/file name, detected domain, ingested_at) is captured - Task 2: Chunking and embedding pipeline (AC: #1, #2, #4) * Implement hybrid chunker (semantic + fixed window fallback) respecting model token limits * Generate embeddings with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-d) and attach to chunk payloads * Normalize text to Markdown and strip unsafe characters before embedding - Task 3: Persistence to stores (AC: #1, #2) * Upsert chunk payload + metadata into PostgreSQL staging tables (if defined) * Write vectors and payload to Qdrant collection knowledge with Cosine distance * Ensure idempotent writes (skip/overwrite via content hash) - Task 4: Observability and error handling (AC: #3) * Add structlog events for start/success/failure with counts and durations * Surface non-zero exit codes for CLI failures; include actionable error messages - Task 5: Tests (AC: all) * Unit tests for chunking logic, format detection, and metadata shaping * Integration test: ingest sample PDF/MD/HTML, verify chunks + embeddings persisted * Integration test: idempotent re-run and failure path (bad file)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Given the user runs `jarvis memory add path/to/file.pdf`, When ingestion completes, Then the file is converted via pandoc, chunked, embedded, and stored with metadata in Qdrant/PostgreSQL. 2. Given ingestion jobs run, When chunking occurs, Then a hybrid strategy (semantic + fixed window) is used and metadata includes source path, section, domain, and timestamps. 3. Given ingestion succeeds or fails, When logs are inspected, Then events show success/failure with file path, chunk counts, and error details. 4. Given supported formats (Markdown, PDF, HTML), When a file of each type is ingested, Then normalized Markdown is produced and embedded with 384-d vectors (all-MiniLM-L6-v2).

doc.title: Epic 2 — Story 2.2
doc.snippet: Pipeline converts uploads to normalized Markdown, embeds chunks with all-MiniLM-L6-v2, and logs ingestion events.

doc.title: Architecture
doc.snippet: Qdrant collection uses 384-d vectors (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), Cosine distance, and HNSW m=16/ef_construct=200/full_scan_threshold=10000.

doc.title: PRD
doc.snippet: Ingestion must normalize Markdown, support multiple formats, and store metadata for retrieval and auditing.

doc.title: Test Design System
doc.snippet: Pytest-based strategy with unit, integration, and slow marks; emphasize fixtures and coverage reporting.

doc.title: Docker Compose
doc.snippet: Qdrant runs on port 6333 with qdrant-data volume for persistence and config mount at docker/qdrant/config.yaml.

artifact.reason: Qdrant client configuration and collection defaults (384-d, Cosine, HNSW) to reuse for ingestion writes.
PostgreSQL connection/session pattern to persist ingestion metadata or staging tables.
Typer CLI pattern and structlog-friendly output; reuse approach for jarvis memory add command.
Mocking approach for Qdrant client and collection operations to model ingestion unit tests.
Integration pattern with live Qdrant, useful for ingestion end-to-end verification.

story-context.constraints: - Use existing Qdrant defaults: 384-d vectors, Cosine distance, HNSW m=16/ef_construct=200/full_scan_threshold=10000 (architecture.md). - CLI patterns should follow Typer/structlog style without logging sensitive content or full document text. - Reuse existing DB/Qdrant client helpers instead of new clients; prefer dependency injection for testability. - Idempotent writes: hash or checksum chunks to avoid duplicate inserts. - Supported formats: Markdown, PDF, HTML; normalize to Markdown via pandoc before chunking/embedding.

tests.standards: Follow docs/test-design-system.md and pytest settings in pyproject.toml; use unit/integration separation and marks for slow tests.
tests.ideas: - AC1/AC4: CLI ingest command converts PDF/HTML/MD, produces normalized Markdown, and exits 0; verify metadata inserted. - AC2: Chunker produces hybrid segments with source path/section/domain/timestamps fields populated. - AC3: Logging includes counts and errors without leaking content; failure path returns non-zero exit. - AC1/AC2: Qdrant payloads stored with 384-d vectors and expected distance metric; idempotent re-run skips duplicates.
